role: wave 4, domain 7 (trail scanners / anchor hunters), R2-measure, defense

prevalence.staticScan: agent2/night/scratch/B067/scanpool.mjs + scanimm.mjs over 926 binaries (693 unique) of official-2025 (online, young, zombies) and cgx2022-2024(y). The only code that compares memory against a far-call tag (1FFFh = FF 1F, or a segment-like word 0F00h-10FFh) is GSA_ido_itay2 (cgx2024 online1/online2/live; not in the 2024 finals). It watches one word 800h above itself, treats it as a pushed IP and checks [IP-2]==FF 1F, so it assumes CS=1000h. 2025 pools: no trail hunter. Other memory scanners are not trail hunters: ORT_Pegasus_Hex2 (looks for any non-CC byte from address 0, then INT 86h), OST_Gamma1 (fixed cells x5A5h/x6A5h of one family), zombie-capture readers of [1243h] (AML_ByteReapers, TOM_2B2Team2), self-check loops (GGN_OpcodeHunter1). V6's own zombie_scan only runs when something writes [7A00h]; no 2025 binary contains the bytes 00 7A.
prevalence.traceReread: agent2/night/scratch/B067/deaths.mjs over the existing trace dirs (pkj3o base, 46uvt, 4sf0x): 4-7% of rev0 deaths are single-word hits on the dwelling anchor (KosherCode1 stride-12 CCCCh bomber, RZL_YANDE1, ELD_FriendlyFire, HRZ_Underflow1, HRZ_MOV_AX_WIN2, GGN_OpcodeHunter1). All of them are blind bombers or copiers, not trail decoders. 84-101 of 161 base deaths are trail overwrites (MOVSW crowd).

counterCodes.label: huntV6
counterCodes.what: Good_Test V6 zombie_scan (friend-provided) run directly as a standalone team. It decodes anchor = W:IP-2 from any trail whose CS word has high byte 0Fh-1Fh (except 0FFCh) and bombs it with CCCCh. Control: hoffA.asm/hoffB.asm (bomb write replaced by nop nop).
counterCodes.strength: y4h5y: hunter team scores 0.261; base 0.333 vs it, against 0.875 vs the no-bomb control huntOff. Different fills, n=6 cohorts each.

counterCodes.label: idoFB
counterCodes.what: Real cgx2024 live GSA_ido_itay pair with one byte patched (add si,-2 -> add si,-52h) so its FF 1F check hits FAR_SEG 0FFBh anchors.
counterCodes.strength: y4h5y: team 0.075 vs 0.025 for the unpatched pair; base 0.717 vs 0.776 (n.s.). Weak, because it watches only a few cells.

candidates.label: hz
candidates.change: A: at startup writes its zombie_entry address to arena cell [4A19h] (lea dx,[si+zombie_entry-start]; mov [4A19h],dx; INT87 moves from instr 10 to 12). The dead V6 zombie_scan tail now skips 0FFBh (own FAR_SEG) instead of 0FFCh. B: zombie_fallback (captured zom20b/d, CX=0) does its counter-bomb INT 87h, then cld; jmp [4A19h], so it runs the trail hunter instead of a phoenix. The zom20a path is unchanged.
candidates.control: hzOff (hzOffA.asm, sha b82b560a9bddfdff; hunter bomb write replaced by nop nop) screen 20261003221300248-B067-screen-xcl3y ALL -0.0373 [-0.0605,-0.0141], 2025 -0.052. Paired hz minus hzOff on the same S cohorts (pair.mjs): ALL +0.0549 [0.0349,0.0748], 2025 +0.0524 [0.0264,0.0785], threat +0.066 [0.023,0.109]. So the hunter's bombs are what makes up for losing the b/d phoenix copies.
candidates.groupNotes: Passes the numeric bar (ALL +0.0176 >= +0.006, multi -0.008 > -0.01), but marginal: the 2025 group is flat, multi is slightly negative over only 2 cohorts, and CodeKiller was -0.15 in the threat job (+0.017 in the screen). The hunting mechanism itself is causally supported (hz minus hzOff +0.055).

threatFindings.threat: A segment-aware far-call trail hunter (decodes W:IP-2 from the pushed trail and bombs the anchor) kills rev0 anchors
threatFindings.evidence: Counter-code huntV6 (V6 zombie_scan standalone), threat y4h5y: rev0 0.333 vs huntV6 and 0.875 vs the identical no-bomb control huntOff (n=6 each, unpaired fills; about -0.54/battle). Hunter team score 0.261 vs 0.008.
threatFindings.impact: Structural for every far-call trail design (rev0, V6 family, zchain4, MOVSW crowd). A FAR_SEG whose high byte is not 0Fh/10h cannot cover the arena, so there is no cheap fix. Realistic cost today is about 0 because no such hunter exists in the pools.

threatFindings.threat: Real archived anchor hunters (GSA_ido_itay2, cgx2024) cost rev0 points
threatFindings.evidence: y4h5y: ido24live team score 0.025, rev0 0.776. It assumes CS=1000h (checks [IP-2]==FF 1F), which misses the 0FFBh trail of rev0, where the anchor is IP-52h. With the 1-byte patch to IP-52h (idoFB) the team scores 0.075 and rev0 0.717 (n.s.): its single-cell watch is too sparse to matter.
threatFindings.impact: ~0. The FAR_SEG offset plus ido's sparse sampling protect rev0.

threatFindings.threat: Trail hunters are common in the 2024/2025 fields
threatFindings.evidence: Static scan of 693 unique 2022-2025 binaries: the only far-call-tag compare is ido_itay2 (2024 online/live). The trace re-read found no deaths from decoded-trail hits; anchor spot hits (4-7% of deaths) come from blind bombers (KosherCode, YANDE, FriendlyFire, Underflow, MOV_AX_WIN, OpcodeHunter1).
threatFindings.impact: 0 of the 2025 teams. Watch any 2026 field for this design.

threatFindings.threat: lead_V6's hunter (zombie_scan behind the [7A00h] redirect) is active against rev0 in the fields
threatFindings.evidence: Static only: no 2025 binary contains the bytes 00 7A, so [7A00h] stays CCCCh and V6 only writes junk at CCCFh-CCD9h. Consistent with B057 (brk24/bqibu). No new job.

threatFindings.threat: Domain-7 hunting used offensively by our own captured zombies (sparing 0FFBh) gains points vs the MOVSW crowd
threatFindings.evidence: hz screen s8pzc +0.0176 [-0.008,0.043]; control hzOff xcl3y -0.037; paired hz-hzOff +0.055 [0.035,0.075]; threat pbt3f cgx +0.088, Baltika9 +0.069 but CodeKiller -0.152 (n=4).
threatFindings.impact: Net +0.018 on S (n.s.). Mechanism +0.055 relative to idle zombies.

recommendation: Defense: no fix proposed. The only effective hunter is purpose-built (huntV6, about -0.54/battle) and appears nowhere in the 2022-2025 pools. The one archived FF 1F hunter (ido_itay) is harmless, helped by FAR_SEG 0FFBh. Keep 0FFBh and keep huntV6 (scratch/B067/huntA/B.asm) as a library threat for future robustness checks. Candidate hz (captured b/d zombies run a hunter that spares our own segment) meets the screen bar (ALL +0.0176) and its mechanism is causally supported (+0.055 vs the hzOff control), but 2025 is flat, multi is -0.008 and CodeKiller was -0.15 in a small threat job. It can go to confirmation as a low-confidence promote-candidate. It is compatible with zph's zom20a-path BP change (zph's 3400h edit becomes moot).
